So, Italy. Home of Michelangelo, half-a-million tiny political parties and the largest combination of high public debt and high debt-to-GDP ratio in Europe.

Until a short while ago, we had a majority rule electoral law: the two parties who came first in Parliamentary elections would compete in a run-off, and the winner would get 53% of the seats in the lower house.

That all changed a few days ago, when our constitutional court ruled the run-off system unconstitutional. Now, instead, the party getting over 40% of the vote will get 53% of the seats, otherwise it's proportional.

Now for the fun part: no party is even close to the 40% threshold, and hasn't been in years. Right now, not only would no single party win a majority, but no foreseeable coalition would win it. Not a German-style grand coalition between cuck left and cuck right, now an anti-euro coalition of euroskeptic parties, nothing. It would basically take 2 of the 3 largest plus 1 of the medium-sized parties to create a majority, except with our politics in its current state no such coalition seems possible: parties would have to ally that pretty much exist to hate each other.

So, this might get fun. The current government could technically go on until 2018, but it's subsisting on a small and fragile majority that might splinter as soon as any of its members feel like that's in the their best interests.
